audit.argument: Claim: when aggressor flow is flat, fade the heavy resting side - an ask-heavy book means price runs UP through it, 'wall = fuel, not floor'. The entire support is one cross-sectional split in legacy_notes.evidence: ask-heavy legs go up 0.61 (n=158), bid-heavy 0.42 (n=121). That number is a real measurement and it is NOT the outcome the play was written to explain, so this is not OUTCOME_CREDITED. It is also not ASSERTED - there is a number and there is a stated mechanism. But it is a single POOLED read over 279 legs from the 12 warm-season days of S92, in direct violation of this desk's standing 'per-cell always, never pool' rule, with no per-cell breakdown, no null, no monotone-in-strength check (which the sibling direction.flow_nowcast does carry), and no replication. The play's own forward field reads 'NONE. Derived on the warm-season set; never re-tested on any later block. Zero forward evidence.' And the same evidence block records 'flow_beats_book_when_disagree 262/293 = 0.89', which scopes the play to the residual 11% of disagreement cases. I cannot classify it higher without a per-cell re-run and I cannot classify it lower without discarding a real measurement, so it is UNCLEAR and I say below exactly what would settle it.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES for the original split - 0.61/0.42 could have come back 0.50/0.50 and did not. NO for anything since: in the entire g17-g23 corpus the play has never been evaluated on a single day, so no test capable of refuting it has been run in five years of walk. The causal story ('wall = fuel') is layered on top of the correlation and was never tested against the obvious alternative (the heavy resting side is where informed capital sits and price is drawn toward it). This project's own OD history is the reason to be careful with exactly this evidence shape: CLAUDE.md records that apparent directional lifts from pooled flow reads 'were trend/base-rate artifacts (Simpson's on a trending window) and died under window/forward sweep + temporal OOS'.
